stem: When evaluating a febrile transplant recipient for possible bacterial infection, which diagnostic study aligns with standard references?

options.text: Blood cultures are never indicated in febrile transplant recipients
Only stool cultures are obtained for every febrile episode
Cultures should be deferred until after two weeks of empiric antibiotics

explanation.rationale_correct: Diagnosis of bacterial infection includes central and peripheral blood cultures, along with cultures of wound, throat, urine, sputum, JP drainage, and/or stool as clinically indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Blood cultures are a standard component of bacterial-infection evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Multiple culture sources may be obtained based on clinical presentation rather than stool alone in every case.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cultures are obtained as part of evaluation, with empiric antibiotics administered after cultures are collected.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → bacterial infection → Diagnosis → g.i.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → bacterial infection → g.i. (central and peripheral blood cultures); PDF p. 734 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Blood-culture diagnostic angle distinct from empiric vancomycin therapy (cctc-3133) and bacterial-sign combo (cctc-3132); anchor verified on Cupples p. 734.

stem: A lung transplant recipient with fever, cough, and decreased breath sounds is being evaluated for bacterial infection. Which diagnostic study aligns with standard references?

options.text: Chest x-ray, particularly in the setting of respiratory symptoms
Chest x-ray is contraindicated in all febrile transplant recipients
Respiratory symptoms require only pulse oximetry without chest imaging
Chest imaging is deferred until bacterial cultures return in two weeks

explanation.rationale_correct: Bacterial infection diagnosis includes chest x-ray particularly in the setting of respiratory symptoms, along with appropriate cultures and clinical assessment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Chest x-ray is specifically recommended with respiratory symptoms rather than being contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.C: Chest x-ray is among cited studies when respiratory symptoms are present.
rationale_incorrect.D: Imaging and cultures are part of early evaluation rather than being deferred for weeks.

stem: A transplant recipient with a central line reports tenderness and erythema at the catheter insertion site with low-grade fever. Which finding aligns with standard bacterial-infection teaching?

options.text: Catheter or tube insertion sites that are erythematous, swollen, and tender
Catheter-site erythema never indicates infection in transplant recipients
Line-site tenderness is expected and requires no evaluation
Only wound dehiscence, never catheter sites, may show infection signs

explanation.rationale_correct: Signs of bacterial infection include catheter or tube insertion sites that are erythematous, swollen, and tender, along with fever and other localized or systemic findings.

rationale_incorrect.B: Catheter-site erythema, swelling, and tenderness are specifically listed infection signs.
rationale_incorrect.C: Catheter-site tenderness with erythema warrants evaluation rather than being dismissed as always expected.
rationale_incorrect.D: Both catheter sites and wound abnormalities may indicate bacterial infection.

stem: A coordinator is updating bacterial-infection diagnostic protocols. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Central and peripheral blood cultures should be obtained.
Chest x-ray is obtained particularly in the setting of respiratory symptoms.
Abdominal CT scan may assess for fluid collections.
Cultures should never be obtained before empiric antibiotics are started.

explanation.rationale_correct: Blood cultures, chest x-ray with respiratory symptoms, and abdominal CT for fluid collections are cited diagnostic steps. Statement IV is false because broad-spectrum antibiotics are administered after cultures are obtained.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—abdominal CT may assess fluid collections.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because cultures are obtained before empiric antibiotics are started.
